note: INVENTED fact patterns for the CE1 coverage registry's exclusion sweeps (review r4 item 9, review r5 item 7). No row is a real person or record. Each worker states, for each fact, the condition texts that are true of the worker: a case holds only when, for every fact in its when, one stated text equals the condition exactly (a boolean equals only the same boolean). expected is the outcome the sources give, decides the case (or residual) that gives it; for a refusing worker, decides is the open case. just_miss_required lists the case conditions (rule, case, fact) for which some worker states every other condition of the case exactly, states a text of its own for that fact, and is decided below the case (review r6 M-1); for the review's drop-free conditions in just_miss_own_text the worker's text for that fact is its own, no case's; just_miss_stated_limits gives the reason none can for the review's drop-free conditions that remain.

workers.worker: INVENTED: Carl, a general partner in a calendar-year partnership, files on a calendar year and dies on 1990-05-10, so his taxable year ends with his death and within the partnership's year. 411(f) includes in his final-year net earnings the part of the deceased partner's distributive share not attributable to any period beginning on or after 1990-06-01, and 411(f)(2) makes the term include his estate's share; the 1985 Form 1040 instructions likewise say a deceased member's distributive share 'must be included in the partner's net earnings'. Read with 411(f)(2) the amount is his distributive share, so partnership_status is false and the residual includes it (NOTE: the text never names 411(f)).
